questions.prompt: Which two properties make computed() efficient?
questions.explanation: A computed signal doesn't run until first read (lazy) and caches its result until a dependency changes (memoized).

questions.prompt: How many times does an effect() run when it is first created?

options.text: At least once, shortly after creation (asynchronously)
Only when read in a template

questions.explanation: Effects are scheduled, not run synchronously: the first run happens during the next change detection, and several changes in a row are batched into one run.

questions.prompt: Copying a value from one signal into another inside an effect() is best replaced by what?
questions.explanation: Deriving state with computed() avoids the ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenChecked errors and extra cycles that state-copying effects cause.

questions.prompt: Which are appropriate use cases for effect()? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Deriving a full name from first and last name signals

questions.explanation: effect() bridges signals to non-reactive APIs; deriving a full name is pure derived state, so it belongs in computed().

questions.prompt: Which function reads a signal's value inside a reactive context WITHOUT registering it as a dependency?
questions.explanation: untracked() lets an effect or computed read a signal without tracking it, avoiding unwanted re-runs.

questions.prompt: Where must effect() be called by default?

options.text: Within an injection context (or pass an explicit Injector)

questions.explanation: effect() needs an injection context so Angular can tie its lifecycle to something; otherwise pass { injector }.
